claim: Cdc42 is a signaling protein important for reorganization of actin cytoskeleton and morphogenesis of cells.
source: Cdc42 is a signaling protein important for reorganization of actin cytoskeleton and morphogenesis of cells.

claim: Postnatal forebrain deletion of Cdc42 leads to deficits in synaptic plasticity.
source: Here we report that postnatal forebrain deletion of Cdc42 leads to deficits in synaptic plasticity and in remote memory recall using conditional knockout of Cdc42.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: Postnatal forebrain deletion of Cdc42 leads to deficits in remote memory recall.
source: Here we report that postnatal forebrain deletion of Cdc42 leads to deficits in synaptic plasticity and in remote memory recall using conditional knockout of Cdc42.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by behavioral test data.

claim: Deletion of Cdc42 impaired LTP in the Schaffer collateral synapses.
source: We found that deletion of Cdc42 impaired LTP in the Schaffer collateral synapses and postsynaptic structural plasticity of dendritic spines in CA1 pyramidal neurons in the hippocampus.
evidence: This finding is stated in the abstract and supported by electrophysiology data in Figure 3E-F.

claim: Deletion of Cdc42 impaired postsynaptic structural plasticity of dendritic spines in CA1 pyramidal neurons in the hippocampus.
source: We found that deletion of Cdc42 impaired LTP in the Schaffer collateral synapses and postsynaptic structural plasticity of dendritic spines in CA1 pyramidal neurons in the hippocampus.
evidence: This finding is stated in the abstract and supported by glutamate uncaging data in Figure 3A-D.

claim: Loss of Cdc42 did not affect memory acquisition.
source: Additionally, loss of Cdc42 did not affect memory acquisition, but instead significantly impaired remote memory recall.
evidence: This finding is stated in the abstract and supported by behavioral data in Figures 5 and 6.

claim: Loss of Cdc42 significantly impaired remote memory recall.
source: Additionally, loss of Cdc42 did not affect memory acquisition, but instead significantly impaired remote memory recall.
evidence: This finding is stated in the abstract and supported by behavioral data in Figures 5 and 6.

claim: The postnatal functions of Cdc42 may be crucial for the synaptic plasticity in hippocampal neurons.
source: Together these results indicate that the postnatal functions of Cdc42 may be crucial for the synaptic plasticity in hippocampal neurons, which contribute to the capacity for remote memory recall.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings presented in the manuscript.

claim: Postnatal Cdc42 functions contribute to the capacity for remote memory recall.
source: Together these results indicate that the postnatal functions of Cdc42 may be crucial for the synaptic plasticity in hippocampal neurons, which contribute to the capacity for remote memory recall.

claim: Fibrous actin (F-actin) creates the underlying cytoskeletal scaffold for neuronal structures.

claim: Dynamic actin turnover in dendritic spines produces morphological and functional changes in synapses.
source: Particularly, the dynamic actin turnover in dendritic spines, the postsynaptic portion of the excitatory synapse, produces morphological and functional changes in synapses (Matus, 1999; Star et al., 2002; Kim et al., 2013), that are thought to be a fundamental basis of synaptic plasticity underlying learning and memory (Kim and Lisman, 1999; Krucker et al., 2000; Fukazawa et al., 2003; Okamoto et al., 2004; Kim et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Small GTPases of the Rho family (Cdc42, Rac, and RhoA) exert distinct roles for actin remodeling by regulating actin organization.

evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Both Cdc42 and Rac promote the formation and maintenance of dendritic spines in vitro.

evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous in vitro studies.

claim: Cdc42f/f mice were crossed with the Camk2a-Cre line to generate conditional knockout mice.
source: To investigate the neuronal morphology and the behavioral outcomes provoked by postnatal Cdc42 disruption in cortical excitatory neurons in vivo, we crossed Cdc42f/f mice with the Camk2a-Cre line, which drives Cre recombinase within pyramidal neurons of the forebrain including the hippocampus and the cerebral cortex by p16-p19 (Tsien et al., 1996).
evidence: This describes the experimental method used to generate the conditional knockout mice.

claim: The Camk2a-Cre line drives Cre recombinase within pyramidal neurons of the forebrain including the hippocampus and the cerebral cortex by p16-p19.
source: To investigate the neuronal morphology and the behavioral outcomes provoked by postnatal Cdc42 disruption in cortical excitatory neurons in vivo, we crossed Cdc42f/f mice with the Camk2a-Cre line, which drives Cre recombinase within pyramidal neurons of the forebrain including the hippocampus and the cerebral cortex by p16-p19 (Tsien et al., 1996).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The total amount of Cdc42 protein in the hippocampus was markedly decreased in Cdc42f/f: Camk2a-Cre mice (p120) compared to control littermates.

claim: The CRIB pulldown assay displayed a substantial reduction of GTP-bound, active Cdc42 in the mutant mice.
source: The CRIB pulldown assay, which was performed using with same amounts of hippocampal lysates from p120 mice, clearly displayed a substantial reduction of GTP-bound, active Cdc42 in the mutant mice, whereas, the total and active form levels of Rac1 were similar both in mutants and controls (Figure 1A).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by CRIB pulldown data in Figure 1A.

claim: The total and active form levels of Rac1 were similar both in mutants and controls.

evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Western blot data in Figure 1A.

claim: Approximately 80% of total Cdc42 protein was lost in mutant hippocampi compared to littermate controls.

claim: CRIB pulldown assays revealed an 85% decrease (15% remained) of active Cdc42 proteins in mutant animals.

claim: There were no changes in total Rac1 and active Rac1 proteins in hippocampi of the mutant mice.
